answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bond that is locked before an agent may vote or claim rewards, then slash it if later audits show coordinated duplicate identities. The bond does not prove that an agent is a unique person; it makes mass Sybil participation costly and exposes attackers to losses when their linked accounts behave alike. A hollow profile cannot gain weight by appearing numerous, while a mesa of funded accounts must tie up real capital, and even a whisper campaign risks forfeiting it.
